reported_status: The Ultra continuation reports conditional all-q stability calculations for a conducting anisotropic skin and moving interface, including a correction for rotation of material axes. It reports that an earlier frozen-axis instability witness does not establish a physical comparison: at the 1 MPa fixture both responsive and ordinary coatings are stable, while a 10 kPa model separates them at one wave number only.

requires_external_validation.scope: Obtain one material with the required joint conductivity, elastic tangent, preload/axis law, contact and stripping measurements, then test a matched full spatial model across all wave numbers and operating costs.

scientific_scope_status: The models use stated constitutive laws, boundary conditions, and loadings. The exact loaded-film tangent, material-axis response, same-film conductivity/modulus conjunction, pore contact/drainage, delamination, loaded constitutive closure, and stable stripping behavior are not acquired. A nonlinear local-column result is not a full spatial conducting-skin theorem. Practical advantage and materials feasibility remain unknown.
